text:
Training many machine learning models together and averaging their predictions can greatly improve accuracy [P3_p1_c02]. However, using such a large group of models at the same time is cumbersome and requires too much computing power for large-scale deployment [P3_p1_c02]. 

Training large models is great for extracting structure from massive datasets, but deploying systems to many users demands speed and low resource use [P3_p1_c03]. This creates a gap between training needs and deployment limits [P3_p1_c03]. 

The paper solves this by using a transfer method called distillation [P3_p1_c03]. Distillation transfers the knowledge from a large, cumbersome model or group of models into a single, smaller model that is much easier to deploy [P3_p1_c02][P3_p1_c03]. 

Regarding accuracy, more than 80% of the accuracy improvement gained by a group of 10 models can be successfully transferred to a single distilled model [P3_p5_c02]. 

As for limitations, specialists that focus on specific fine-grained classes can tend to overfit because their effective training set is much smaller [P3_p1_c02][P3_p8_c02]. Also, a group of models gives a smaller improvement on the ultimate objective of word error rate due to a mismatch in the target function [P3_p5_c02].
